artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: The bd-tree bronze module. Two modes: `discover` (the ONE ledgered discovery read) and `pull` (the qt4 selection, run, poll, export, dedup and bronze write). No schedule was built -- the spec for one is section 5 of the result doc, per the order. Deterministic and re-runnable, which is the MECHANISM half of the vendor-egress grant (R-21 @b390c36444): the pull lives in a script, never in an agent turn.

12,132 rows, one per asset_id (unique True, 0 nulls), 15 columns, as-of 09/25/2026. DEPLOYED-VERIFIED because AC2 read it back from S3 with its own downloader and head-object, not from the local build buffer: LastModified 2026-09-28T05:24:16Z is after the issuance at 2026-09-28T04:25:12Z, and the uniqueness bar was evaluated on the served bytes.
Three ledgered vendor operations with the authority record printed and verified at its pin, the super-class outcome as a dim id, and the declared overrun of the order's two-call bound.

OUTPUT_KEY as the first data line (AC2 parses it), the row count, the super-class outcome, the step-1.1 allocation answer, the scheduling spec, the union coverage note with both counts, and the departures.

The machine record of the discovery read: roster of 19 templates, the qt4 catalog's 8 levels / 201 dimensions, the super-class hit with its scan denominator, and a present/ABSENT verdict per required dim id.

acceptance.status_reason: PASSES AT 3, NOT 2, AND THE THIRD IS THE DISCLOSURE: the order's bound 2 allows at most two BD calls and this seat made three. The first pull attempt fired run 541481 server-side and was not parsed (BD returns the run either wrapped in "template" or at the top level; only the wrapped shape was handled), so no export was taken. On a first run this criterion read calls=2 because that row's timestamp carried an 'x' placeholder the check's regex cannot match -- i.e. the check PASSED while being blind to the very call being disclosed. The timestamp was made machine-parseable and the row now carries the claim `inferred` on its time, since the seat did not record the failed attempt's clock.

mutant.description: The spec names no mutant control. The controls that carried weight were falsification controls on the reads and on a refactor.
mutant.observed: Three ran. (1) REFACTOR CONTROL: after moving scope, vendor, firm short-code, secret and bucket from literals to registry reads, the derived values were asserted equal to the four the live pull actually used -- so the naming fix is provably behaviour-preserving rather than assumed to be. (2) DROP CONTROL: before removing the duplicate raw 'Asset SuperClass' column from the served object, the two columns were asserted identical value-for-value; the drop was conditional on that assertion. (3) RENAME CONTROL: the value distribution was asserted unchanged across the asset_super_class_bd -> asset_super_class rename.

determinism.method: The pull is one live vendor read of changing production state, so it is not re-runnable to an identical byte image by construction. The checks are.
determinism.observed: All three AC scripts returned the same verdict on repeat within the session. AC3 was run twice deliberately and changed 2 -> 3 only because the ledger's disclosure was made machine-visible, not because the world moved.
